description:
Watch this clip from the State of Unreal at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 to explore all the latest news on the Epic Games Store and what’s coming down the pipe.

2025 was a year of growth for the Epic Games Store, setting us up for a strong 2026. Players spent $1.16 billion in the store across 1P and 3P titles, a 6% increase year over year. Our programs are still going strong including Launch Everywhere With Epic, Epic First Run and Epic Rewards.

For a full roundup on all the announcements at the State of Unreal, check out our blog post: https://www.unrealengine.com/news/state-of-unreal-2026-top-news-from-the-show

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Watch this clip from the State of Unreal at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 to learn about Lore, Epic’s next-generation open source version control system. 

We decided to build Lore from scratch, designing the data model to meet our requirements from the ground up. We made scalability and performance core tenets from day one.

We’re releasing Lore as open source today. All source code, along with documentation of data formats and protocols are released under an MIT license and free to use. This release should not be viewed as a complete package, but as an invitation to you to extend it, challenge it, and help shape it into something even more powerful, together.

Find out more: Lore.org

#Lore, #VersionControl, #UnrealEngine5.8, #UE5.8
title: Lore: Next-Generation Version Control | State of Unreal | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026

Watch this video to see the impressive digital character work being created with MetaHuman by talented teams around the world.

As the MetaHuman framework becomes more powerful, we’re seeing some fantastic examples of just how far it’s possible to push the technology. 

The projects in this video span industries as diverse as games, film & TV, animation, broadcast & live events, and beyond. Take a look and get a glimpse at what you can achieve with MetaHuman.

Want to start creating your own realistic digital humans? Check out our website: metahuman.com.

description: Join Vitalii Boiko as he discusses the systems that power DDoD and the decisions that shaped its development. Learn how procedural generation, multiplayer architecture, analytics, and player feedback informed both the game's design and production process.  Hear firsthand how a small team balanced design, technology, testing, and marketing to bring their project to life.
